systems.name: 5/4 Vamp Pulse
systems.description: Feel five as a repeatable 3+2 vamp rather than a counting problem.

systems.name: Minor Pentatonic Guardrail
systems.description: Canonical rectangle and stack topology for minor pentatonic.

learner_needs.name: Stop freezing when the bar has five beats
Keep the melody from floating away from the pulse
Understand harmony from voicing content rather than external charts

moments.title: Feel Five As A Vamp, Not A Math Problem
moments.description: Play the rhythm shell on beats 1-5 while saying long-short.

moments.title: Put The Melody On Top Of The Vamp
moments.description: Play only the first melody target in each measure against the rhythm shell.

moments.title: Let The Rhythm Track Name The Chords
moments.description: Strum each shell and name chord tones before reading an inferred symbol.

moments.title: Odd-Meter Pickup Placement
moments.description: Count 1-2-3-4-5 and enter on the written pickup beat.

play_this.title: Play This: Five Without Freezing
play_this.opening: PLAY THIS. Strum the rhythm shell five times per bar and say long-short.
play_this.ending: So now you know what to do when five-four makes your hand stop.

play_this.title: Play This: Melody Targets Over The Vamp
play_this.seed: First melody target in each measure, measures 1-8
play_this.opening: PLAY THIS. Keep the vamp going in your ear and play only the melody targets.
play_this.ending: So now you know where the melody lands inside five.

play_this.title: Play This: Name The Shell Before The Chord
play_this.opening: PLAY THIS. Strum the shell and name the notes before saying the chord name.
play_this.ending: So now you know how to trust the voicing before the chart.

claims.text: Highlander prioritizes chord-tone awareness before color.
Highlander prioritizes voice-leading and target-tone behavior before pattern collection.
Teach diminished arpeggio skeleton before whole-half scale.

relationships.notes: The Play This inventory explicitly proposes adding the melody skeleton after the rhythm shell.
The rhythm shell is the shared playable seed for naming its chord tones.
